name: Barclays
seo_title: Barclays interview process: what to expect
description: What Barclays' own careers pages say about its online assessments, assessment centre and interviews, each line linked to its source.
intro: This guide sums up what Barclays's own careers pages say about applying and interviewing, from how to apply to experienced hires. It reflects those pages as we checked them on 16 October 2026. Processes differ by programme, role and country, so check Barclays's careers site for your role before you apply.

items.text: For its internships and graduate programmes, Barclays says the first step is completing the application form on its careers site.
Barclays says you can apply for only one full-time graduate or internship role worldwide each year, and if you send several applications only the first is considered.
Barclays says it fills open vacancies on a rolling, first-come-first-served basis, so it recommends applying early.
Barclays says you do not need a finance-related degree to work there: it is more interested in who you are than what you studied, although certain roles do need a more technical degree.
Barclays asks internship and graduate applicants to say in their application if they need adjustments, and says past adjustments include extra time for assessments and offline assessments.

For its internships and graduate programmes, Barclays says the initial assessments are two short interactive assessments about how you might perform at work and your typical or preferred ways of working, which you can take on any device, including a phone or tablet.
Barclays says that for more technical programmes, such as the Explorer Developer programme, it asks candidates to complete an assessment of their technical skills.

For its internships and graduate programmes, Barclays says that, where possible, it hosts most of its assessments on a digital experience platform, which also has hints and tips and some practice tests.
For online assessments, Barclays advises reading the instructions carefully and completing all the practice and example questions.

For its internships and graduate programmes, Barclays says candidates who pass the earlier steps are invited to an assessment centre, either in person or online, as a further chance to show the strengths, behaviours or technical skills the role needs.
Barclays says its internship and graduate assessment centre has two or three stages, including a motivational interview with a member of the leadership team.
Barclays says third-party AI tools, including transcription bots and meeting assistants, are not allowed during its interviews.
Barclays says using such a tool will end your interview and withdraw your application, and may affect whether you can apply for future roles at Barclays.
For its internships and graduate programmes, Barclays says its assessments look at whether you share the key qualities and Values of Barclays colleagues.
Barclays names its Values as Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence and Stewardship, and its Mindset as Empower, Challenge and Drive.
On its listing for the Capital Markets Graduate Programme 2027 in London, Barclays lists the qualities it looks for as resilient, adaptable, confident, driven, empathetic and curious.
Barclays says it does not choose people on academic record alone, and asks applicants to tell it about their extra-curricular activities and work experience.
Barclays advises backing up your application answers with clear examples of judgement, innovation, teamwork, commitment and leadership, and avoiding clichés or claims you cannot prove.
Barclays suggests organising mock interviews with family or friends to build confidence in answering unexpected questions.
In its interview tips, Barclays suggests using a laptop or computer with a high-quality camera if you can, although a phone will do.
Barclays advises researching the company, the business area and the specific role or programme before your interview.
Barclays says that if you feel one exercise went badly you should not give up, because it takes your performance across all of them into account.

For experienced hires, Barclays says interviews for some roles might include extra assessments such as role plays, case studies and presentations, that it assesses only skills relevant to the role, and that it gives a full brief beforehand.
For experienced hires, Barclays says its online assessments can take up to an hour, that you can always practise first, and that reaching the minimum score is the minimum requirement for the job.
In its Professional Candidate Preparation Guide (July 2024), Barclays suggests using the STAR method (situation, task, action, result) to structure interview answers.

sources.title: Capital Markets Graduate Programme 2027 London at Barclays
Global Hiring Framework: Professional Candidate Preparation Guide (July 2024, V1.0)

practice_advice: Practise explaining a client situation and your recommendation out loud in a few minutes, with the answer first and then your reasons.
Keep a short list of business stories you have followed, and practise saying what each one means for a company and its bank.
Do short, timed mental maths drills most days: the numbers in a case study are easier when the arithmetic is automatic.
